Level ladder — what each level contains

A preview made by applying the rules in the level ladder design (spec §7.2) to today's curriculum files. The ladder is not built yet, so this is a test run, not the final ladder.

How to read this page
  • Kanji, radicals, words: placed with the spec rules (greedy kanji order; 18 / 24 / 28 / 30 kanji per level; radical at its first kanji; word at the later of its last kanji and its frequency slot). The real build (Task 2) can give different numbers.
  • Grammar: decided by the spec. The 126 N5+N4 points keep today's teaching order and spread over levels 1–20 (about 6 per level). The 34 N3 points spread over levels 21–25. Nothing after level 25 has grammar.
  • Passages: the spec says 60 new passages, about 3 per level, over levels 2–20. They are not written yet, so each one is an empty slot here. The split of the 3 extra passages is my guess. Level 1 and levels 21–60 have no passages. (For comparison: today's 60 passages, measured on this ladder, would land at level 13: 2, level 14: 1, level 15: 9, level 16: 2, level 17: 6, level 20: 3, level 21: 1, level 22: 7, level 23: 16, level 24: 13.)
  • Highlights (spec §7.6), measured on this test ladder: solid pink = work before release: kanji and radicals in levels 1–20 with no mnemonic (write new), grammar points whose pool sentences, linked words or mnemonic example use a later word or kanji (regenerate; the reason is under each point), and all passages (write new). dashed blue = work in the later phase: words whose example sentences use a later word, or whose mnemonic was written without its kanji. Levels 21–60 are a skeleton, so a missing mnemonic there is not marked. The grammar mnemonic check looks at kanji only, so it can miss a later kana-only word.
  • WaniKani (grey, at the bottom of each level): the same level number in WaniKani, from the private reference file. Kanji that are also in our level have the kanji colour. Hover a WaniKani kanji to see where our ladder puts it. Radicals that WaniKani shows only as a picture appear as their name. This is for your own comparison only: do not share or commit this page.
  • JLPT label: display only. Measured with today's N5/N4 files as the reference lists: N5 range = levels 1–16, N4 range = levels 17–24.
